papers.title: Characterization and understanding of mechano-chemical degradation of polypropylene and chlorinated polyvinyl chloride in semiconductor wastewater environments
papers.abstract: The degradation behaviors of polypropylene (PP) and chlorinated polyvinyl chloride (cPVC) in H 2 O 2 and SC-1 solutions at various concentrations and temperatures were investigated. Because H 2 O 2 and SC-1 solutions are inherently unstable, a custom-designed apparatus was developed to maintain constant solution concentration and temperature during accelerated degradation. Chemical characterization using FT-IR spectroscopy and XPS revealed that degradation reactions proceeded more extensively in cPVC than in PP. While hydroxyl radical-induced hydrogen abstraction initiated degradation in most cases, cPVC exposed to SC-1 predominantly followed a dehydrochlorination-induced oxidation mechanism. Tensile testing showed that PP exhibited a significant reduction in toughness only under the most severe condition at 60 °C, whereas cPVC experienced toughness degradation under all test conditions. In SC-1 environments, the normalized toughness of cPVC approached zero, accompanied by an approximately 40% reduction in yield strength and a decrease in tensile modulus, indicating severe embrittlement. SEM observations revealed the formation of small surface cracks that promoted local stress concentration and contributed to the pronounced loss of toughness. Based on an integrated analysis of the experimental results, the degradation mechanisms of each material were proposed, and the relationships between the observed chemical and mechanical changes were discussed.

papers.title: Selective laser sintering of soft and hard magnetic polymer composites with programmable magnetization
papers.abstract: Four-dimensional (4D) printing of magnetic composites enables adaptive systems responsive to external magnetic fields; however, achieving programmable magnetic functionality and multi-material integration in additively manufactured structures remains challenging. This work presents a selective laser sintering (SLS) approach for fabricating programmable magnetic polymer composites with tunable properties. Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) powders were combined with NdFeB, AlNiCo, or FeSi particles (10–50 wt%), enabling systematic control of magnetic and mechanical behavior. NdFeB-based composites exhibited intrinsic coercivity up to 585 kA/m and energy products up to 2200 J/m 3 , while AlNiCo composites showed a coercivity of 57 kA/m. FeSi composites demonstrated soft magnetic behavior with negligible coercivity and saturation up to 70 kA/m. Mechanical testing revealed Young’s modulus between 2.4 and 3.3 MPa, and nano-computed tomography confirmed uniform particle distribution with volume fractions up to 11.6%. The novelty of this work lies in: First, multi-material integration is achieved within a single printed structure, as demonstrated through proof-of-concept electro-permanent magnets (173 mm 3 ) exhibiting bistable switching with an ON/OFF force ratio of 5.75 and magnetically actuated membranes exhibiting displacements up to 2.8 µm. Second, spatial control of magnetic response is demonstrated through controlled magnetization, enabling defined magnetization profiles in soft folding structures inspired by gripper behavior.

papers.title: A switchable nanozyme with microenvironment-responsive ROS regulation for synergistic antitumor therapy
papers.abstract: The clinical translation of nanocatalytic therapy is frequently hampered by the nonspecific “always-on” catalytic activity of conventional nanozymes, which risks off-target oxidative damage to healthy tissues. To overcome this limitation, we engineered a novel FePd alloy nanozyme (FPAN) with tumor microenvironment (TME)-responsive switchable catalysis. Under physiological conditions, FPAN exhibits catalase (CAT)- and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities that scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS), providing cytoprotection and anti-inflammatory effects. In the acidic and H 2 O 2 -rich TME, it switches to potent peroxidase (POD)-like activity, efficiently generating cytotoxic •OH for chemodynamic therapy (CDT). This therapeutic effect is synergistically enhanced by an intrinsic photothermal response under 808 nm irradiation. FPAN achieved potent tumor ablation through synergistic photothermal-CDT tumor metastasis inhibition in vivo with excellent biocompatibility and protected normal hepatocytes. This work presents FPAN as a promising nanotherapeutic candidate. It enables precise tumor treatment with anti-inflammatory and anti-metastasis benefits. Furthermore, it establishes a versatile design paradigm for smart, adaptive nanomaterials.

papers.title: Ultrasonic welding vs. reflow soldering: Reliability of Cu terminal joints on AMB substrates for EV power modules
papers.abstract: In this study, Cu terminal joints on Si 3 N 4 -based active metal brazing (AMB) substrates for electric vehicle power modules were investigated to compare ultrasonic welding and reflow soldering across three substrate conditions: Cu A (C1020 oxygen-free Cu), Cu B (C1011 oxygen-free Cu), and electroless Ag-plated Cu B. The ultrasonic joints formed a continuous Cu–Cu direct bonding structure without a distinct interface, accompanied by severe interfacial plastic deformation and grain refinement. The Cu B substrate exhibited a broader HAGB distribution, suggesting more advanced recrystallization-related microstructural evolution compared with the Cu A and electroless Ag conditions. In contrast, soldered joints exhibited Cu 6 Sn 5 and Ag 3 Sn intermetallic compounds (IMCs), with coarsened Ag 3 Sn prominently formed on the electroless Ag substrate. Mechanically, the ultrasonic joints generally showed higher mean shear strength than the reflowed-soldered joints across all substrate conditions, with the highest strength observed for the Cu B substrate, associated with its higher interfacial HAGB fraction and twin-containing microstructure. Overall, ultrasonic welding eliminates solder-derived IMC formation by forming a direct Cu–Cu joint without a solder layer while maintaining a stable metallic current-conduction path, demonstrating strong potential as a terminal bonding technology for high-temperature, high-power EV power modules.

papers.title: Optimization of double-sided CFRE patch repairs on Al 7075-T6 alloy using Taguchi method
papers.abstract: This study models and optimizes three independent repair parameters: patch shape (circle, rectangle, triangle, ellipse, and rhombus), adhesive thickness (100, 150, 200, 250, and 300 µm), and number of plies (1-ply, 2-ply, 3-ply, 4-ply, and 5-ply) for unidirectional Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Epoxy (CFRE) double-sided patch repair of Al 7075-T6 alloy. A five-level, three-factor ( L 25 ) Taguchi design was used to identify optimal parameter values, given their critical role in the repair mechanism. Three-dimensional (3-D) finite element simulations were performed using a combined Extended Finite Element Method (XFEM) and Cohesive Zone Modeling (CZM) approach to simulate crack propagation and adhesive failure. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) indicated that patch shape and number of plies most significantly influenced apparent fracture toughness ( K app ), while adhesive thickness had a minor effect. The optimal double-sided repair configuration was a rectangular patch with 100 µm adhesive thickness and a 5-ply CFRE patch, yielding a predicted K app of 38.32 (±2.30) MPa√m. Experimental validation demonstrated the reliability of the analytical model, with a negligible error of 0.9%. This optimized repair increased K app by 50.4% compared to the unrepaired specimen.
